text:
emily: Quick question — running into a weird combo: our Node SDK client is pointed at a private VPC endpoint via REDWOOD_BASE_URL (https://internal-rw.company.local) but my laptop also has HTTP_PROXY set for corporate egress. Requests are failing TLS handshake when the proxy tries to connect to the internal host. Which should the SDK prioritize? do we have a recommended pattern for local dev + proxy?

raj: The short answer: base URL determines where the SDK tries to connect; proxy envs (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) determine whether the outbound connection is routed through a proxy. If the proxy is in the path to your private endpoint and cannot reach it, you'll need to bypass the proxy for that host (NO_PROXY) or use a hostname that the proxy can resolve/reach. SDK doesn't override system proxy behavior.

marta: Adding a few concrete notes:
- If REDWOOD_BASE_URL is an IP (https://10.4.2.3) then SNI during TLS handshake will be the IP, certs usually don't have that in SAN -> cert validation fails. Prefer a hostname that matches the cert (internal-rw.company.local).
- Most OSs/libs honor NO_PROXY/NO_PROXY_LIST, so set NO_PROXY=internal-rw.company.local,10.4.0.0/16 locally.

raj: Example Node snippets we recommend for local dev:

1) env approach (quick):
```
# bash
export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://internal-rw.company.local
export NO_PROXY=internal-rw.company.local,10.4.0.0/16
# keep your normal HTTP_PROXY for external requests
```

2) programmatic override if you need to force direct connection (Node):
```js
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const https = require('https');

const agent = new https.Agent({
  keepAlive: true,
  // explicitly disable proxy usage for this agent if your app uses a global proxy lib
});

const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseURL: 'https://internal-rw.company.local',
  httpAgent: agent,
});
```
Note: some proxy libraries (e.g., global-tunnel, proxy-agent) will still intercept; the NO_PROXY env is usually the least invasive fix.

tim: Python nuance: requests + requests-ntlm + corporate proxies sometimes rewrite CONNECT and break SNI. If you see handshake errors in Python but Node works, check whether your app is injecting a corporate CA or a MITM proxy. For TLS validation you can also point to the right CA with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or set verify to the CA bundle path in tests.

marta: Another gotcha — CORS for browser-based SDK usage. If you try to point browser JS directly at a private VPC hostname, the browser will enforce CORS and also won't honor NO_PROXY. Browsers always use the system proxy; to reach private endpoints from browser you need either: (a) a reverse-proxy in your dev network that the browser can reach, or (b) run the client through a server-side proxy that you control.

raj: If folks want the SDK to automatically bypass proxies for known VPC hostnames, that's a potential feature. We have an open PR draft to add explicit REDWOOD_BYPASS_PROXY (boolean or host list) so SDK can short-circuit proxy agent creation. Filing an RFC would help decide defaults. I can open a follow-up PR.

devex-bot: Docs: https://intranet.redwood.dev/devex/vpc-endpoints#proxy-and-baseurl (internal) — contains examples for NO_PROXY, CI setups, and certificate troubleshooting.

emily: Thanks — immediate fix was adding NO_PROXY and using internal hostname instead of IP. Two follow-ups: 1) can someone add a one-liner to the Node quickstart about NO_PROXY? 2) is there a CI-friendly pattern to run tests against private endpoint from GH actions (self-hosted runner vs port-forward)?

tim: For CI we recommend using a self-hosted runner inside the VPC or set up a temporary SSH tunnel in the workflow:
```
# example GH actions step (very simple)
- name: open tunnel
  run: ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:12345:internal-rw.company.local:443 jumpbox@jump.internal
- name: run tests
  env:
    REDWOOD_BASE_URL: https://127.0.0.1:12345
    REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE: ./internal-ca.pem
  run: npm test
```
Otherwise a dedicated CI runner in the VPC is more robust.

raj: Summary / checklist for anyone hitting this:
- prefer hostname (matches cert SAN) over raw IP
- set NO_PROXY for internal host ranges
- for browser workloads use a reachable reverse-proxy or server-side mediate
- for CI prefer self-hosted runners in VPC or SSH port-forward with CA bundle
- open PR if you want SDK-level REDWOOD_BYPASS_PROXY support (I'll take it)

emily: Perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
